answer: A protocol can require every identity to lock a scarce token deposit before voting on reputation or earning rewards. The deposit is an anchor: if a challenge proves an identity is fake or part of a colluding cluster, its stake is slashed. A gale of Sybil accounts then costs the attacker real capital for each identity, which remains at risk rather than being created for free. Changing names like a willow in wind does not help if each account still needs its own locked stake.
